theorem_title: Prime setup fits the executed arithmetic budget
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandPrimeCosts.setup_time_le_budget {n R : ℕ} (k : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (hR : R ≤ 3*_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.CostLedger.bandCount n^2) :
    _root_.ThreeSum.LightBandPrimeSetup.time (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ArithmeticStageBounds.maxMod n) (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandScales.bandSize n) R (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Scales.radix n) (_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.primeWindow n) (n^k) ≤
      _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandPrimeCosts.timeBudget k n := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
For natural $k$, positive input length $n$, and record count $R\le3\operatorname{bandCount}(n)^2$, the actual band-prime setup time at the schedule modulus, band size, radix, window, and input bound $n^k$ is at most $\operatorname{timeBudget}(k,n)$.

This estimate accounts for every executed prime-setup component inside the arithmetic term of the runtime ledger.
